Class TaskService

java.lang.Object
io.mcs.taskmanager.services.TaskService
@Service public class TaskService extends Object
Tasks: adding, listing, changing and deleting them. A task needs a title that is not blank, and a status. The title and description are trimmed, and kept within Task.MAX_TITLE_CHARACTERS and Task.MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARACTERS. A new task starts TaskStatus.PENDING. A task that no longer exists, deleted in another copy of the app that has the same database open, is refused by every change with a message saying so, never an error.

Each method is one transaction: a change the app will not make throws Refused and saves nothing of it. The tasks returned are no longer attached to the database; change one through this service, never by its setters.

Author:
Hamza Rasool, Abdullah Khan

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public List<Task> list()

    • search

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public List<Task> search(@Nullable String text, @Nullable TaskStatus status)
      The tasks whose title or description holds the text, whatever its case, in one status or in all. Every character typed is matched as it is: % and _ are not wildcards.
      Parameters:
      text - what to look for, trimmed; null or blank to match every task
      status - the one status to list, or null for every status
      Returns:
      the matching tasks, newest first; empty when none match

    • set

      private static void set(Task task, @Nullable String title, @Nullable String description)
      Sets the task's title and description, trimmed, refusing a blank title and a text over its limit. The limits are counted after trimming, so spaces typed around a text never push it over.
      Parameters:
      task - the task to set them on
      title - what is to be done
      description - more about it; null for none
      Throws:
      Refused - if the title is blank, or the title or the description is too long

    • containing

      private static String containing(String text)
      A like pattern matching any text that holds this one, in lower case so the search ignores case. The pattern's own wildcards, and ! which escapes them, are escaped so each is matched as typed.
      Parameters:
      text - what to look for; empty to match everything
      Returns:
      the pattern, such as %report%
